definition: Rout means an overwhelming, decisive defeat — especially one that ends in a disorderly, chaotic retreat.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rout. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rout should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The invasion collapsed into a rout when the panicked soldiers threw down their shields and fled in every direction.
A defeat can be narrow and hard-fought, but a rout is so one-sided that the losing side simply falls apart.
A rout scatters the losing side in disorder; an annihilation implies it was wiped out completely.

A drubbing is a one-sided beating, usually on a scoreboard — the losing team takes its lumps and goes home. A rout adds collapse: the losing side comes apart, its order dissolving into flight. Every rout would count as a drubbing; not every drubbing has the panic.

A trouncing is a thorough, overwhelming defeat, and the word watches the winner — how completely they dominated. A rout watches the loser: the moment resistance stops being resistance, lines break, and everyone runs. You trounce an opponent who keeps playing; you rout one who falls apart.

Shellacking is the informal, joking word for a decisive, humiliating loss — talk-radio and locker-room language. Rout is the standard word that military historians and sportswriters share, and it carries a precise image the slang lacks: a side so beaten it scatters in disorder.

It also works as a verb: 'the champions routed their rivals.' Don't confuse it with route (a path or way) — one letter apart, completely unrelated meaning.
